name: Rudolf Igor
role: Product owner of the web shop
style: Says awkward things that people do not say at work: too much private detail, strange remarks about colleagues, sudden changes of topic, odd suspicions (somebody moves his chair, an issue looks at him). The request itself is always clear.

name: Ewa Mazur
style: Precise and polite. Uses 'proszę', issue keys and exact status names. Short full sentences.

name: Daniel Brooks
style: Polish with English words (bump, ticket, label). Lower case, no full stops, 'pls' and 'thx'.

name: Zofia Kaczmarek
style: Tells what customers say. Describes the problem in words and does not know issue keys. Long, kind sentences.

name: Marta Pawlak
role: Product manager of the mobile app
style: Very short commands without greetings. Often names a deadline or the release.

name: Kamil Dudek
style: Casual spoken Polish: 'ogarnij', 'wrzuć', 'siema'. Lower case, sometimes no Polish letters.

name: Sophie Grant
style: Very polite. Writes careful Polish with English technical terms. Thanks for each action.

name: Tomasz Baran
style: Technical and dry. Gives the technical background of the request, then the exact action.

name: Oliver Hayes
style: Mixes Polish and English in one sentence. Talks about partners and endpoints.

name: Natalia Zając
style: Talks about the sprint, the planning and the team. Friendly, uses 'zespole' and 'dziękuję'.

name: Joanna Kurek
style: Business context first (management, a report, a deadline). Asks for numbers.

name: Igor Kwiatkowski
style: One short line. Minimum of words, no greetings.

name: Priya Raman
style: Polite Polish with English data terms (pipeline, dashboard, dataset).

name: Karolina Bielecka
style: Urgent tone. Short sentences, sometimes capital letters or exclamation marks during incidents.

name: Wojciech Michalak
style: Formal, old style: 'uprzejmie proszę', 'Szanowni'. Long correct sentences.

name: Ethan Cole
style: Mostly English jargon inside Polish sentences (on-call, alert, rollback).
